subject: P95 & Streaming Qualification for Aperture Health — Proposed Next Steps
messages:
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>

Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 5 Oct 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: P95 & Streaming Qualification for Aperture Health — Proposed Next Steps

Thanks for your time today, Lena — great discussion. Below is a concise capture of the pain points, target success criteria we agreed on, and proposed next steps for the PoC so we can scope resources and timelines. Please flag anything I missed.

Key pain points (what you told us)
- Intermittent spikes pushing models beyond existing capacity, causing user-facing stalls during live sessions.
- Streaming UX degrades when concurrency climbs above ~120 concurrent interactive sessions.
- Lack of detailed tail-latency visibility (only aggregate p50/p90 today) — hard to correlate infra events to UX regressions.

Current stack snapshot (what you shared)
- Inference: On-prem Triton cluster (4x A100s), model served as a single monolith, CPU-bound request queuing.
- Orchestration: Internal autoscaler that reacts slowly to burst traffic (30–90s).
- Observability: Prometheus + Grafana; no per-request token-level tracing or streaming time-to-first-byte metrics.

Success criteria for an initial PoC
- P95 end-to-end latency for streaming responses <= 300ms at target concurrency (see below).
- Support sustained concurrency of 250 interactive sessions with acceptable cost envelope.
- Streaming behavior: time-to-first-byte < 100ms and steady chunked output without stalls.
- Observable metrics and traces that map tokens->model->host for incident triage.

Quantitative targets you asked to validate
- Baseline target concurrency: 250 concurrent interactive sessions (each ~1 request/sec during peak).
- P95 target: <= 300ms overall; TTFB target: <= 100ms.

Proposed PoC plan (timeline & deliverables)
1) Pre-PoC: exchange load profile and a short sample dataset (you) — by 2026-10-09.
2) Redwood runs a bench: synthetic load (our load_test_script.sh) against a mirrored model variant in our hosted sandbox to validate latency envelope — 3 business days.
3) Joint run: deploy a dedicated test pool in your VPC or a private peered environment to reproduce streaming UX under realistic network conditions — 1 week.
4) Deliverable: report with p50/p90/p95, TTFB distribution, KV cache hit rate, recommended batching/quantization profile, and an SLA draft for production handoff.

Immediate asks from Redwood
- Can you share a representative 48-hour traffic sample + a couple of transcripts? (we only need low-sensitivity examples)
- Point person for firewall/VPC peering logistics (we noted Victor as procurement; who will own the tech side?)

Attachments: PoC plan PDF, load_test_script.sh, initial SLA draft (attached).

Next steps: If the above looks right, I'll get Rishi and Marissa to schedule a 30–45 minute technical runbook sync to align on telemetry and endpoints. Proposed windows: 2026-10-07 10:00–11:00 PT or 2026-10-07 14:00–15:00 PT.

Thanks again — excited to move quickly.

—
Stephanie Nguyen
Solutions Lead, Redwood Inference

- Data: we can share redacted transcripts and a 48-hour traffic histogram by 2026-10-08.

Confirmations / asks
- Tech contact for peering: Samira Patel (samira.patel@aperturehealth.com) — she will own the VPC/peering configuration.
- Procurement loop: Victor will handle contract and procurement questions; he asked for an initial SLA and an indicative monthly cost range for a dedicated test pool to present to finance.

Thanks Lena — added Samira and Victor to the thread. A few technical notes ahead of the sync to help Samira and your infra team prepare: 

What we'll need from Aperture for a VPC-peered PoC
- A short-lived test subnet and IAM role for our runner, or an agreed SSH bastion + allowed CIDR list for our sandbox.
- Example model artifact (or a lightweight mirrored variant) — we can also run a synthetic proxy if artifact transfer is restricted.
- A light-weight endpoint for TTFB tracing (we'll deploy a small sidecar to emit per-request markers).

What Redwood will do during bench and joint run
- Run continuous streaming scenarios at increasing concurrency (50, 125, 250, 400) and capture p50/p90/p95 and chunked TTFB distributions.
- Collect KV cache hit/miss, GPU utilization, and scheduling latency breakdowns.
- Produce recommended tuning: batch sizes, KV cache warm strategies, and quantization profile suggestions for cost tradeoffs.

Pre-sync deliverable: I'll drop a short checklist and the load_test_script.sh into the shared Drive link so Samira can validate network access before the meeting.

If you have any special compliance constraints for artifacts (e.g., no model outbound), tell us and we will run the test entirely in your VPC via a temporary runner.

—
